  • The Zammad service runs four processes: the web server, the web application, the WebSocket server, and the background worker. Together they request about 1 CPU and 2 GiB of memory, before PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch, and the other services.
  • Set Administrator email on the Zammad app service. It is required. See the next section.

A new app takes a few minutes before its domain answers, while Zammad installs its database.

docs.title: Administrator account
docs.text:
Set the first administrator in the Zammad service's settings when you create the app:

Setting What it sets Administrator email The email address the administrator signs in with. Required. Administrator first name The administrator's first name. Admin by default. Administrator last name The administrator's last name.

Wodby generates the password as the admin_password token. During the first deployment, before Zammad serves any page, Wodby creates the administrator with the Admin and Agent roles and access to all groups. Zammad's getting started page, which lets the first visitor create the administrator, is never offered.

  1. Open the Zammad app service's Configuration > Tokens tab and reveal admin_password. See Tokens.
  2. Open the app's main domain and sign in with Administrator email and that password.
  3. Change the password under Profile, then set your organization name and connect your mailboxes.

The settings and the token are used only while no administrator exists. Changing them later does not change an existing administrator; change it in Zammad under Profile or Admin > Users.

If the email already belongs to another Zammad user, the administrator is not created and the deployment does not finish. Set another email and deploy again.

Customers can register themselves by default (Register as a new customer). Turn this off under Admin > Security > Base if customers must not sign up.

docs.title: Search with Elasticsearch
docs.text:
Zammad uses Elasticsearch for search. It needs a supported Elasticsearch version, and the catalog Elasticsearch service provides one. OpenSearch is not supported by Zammad. See Zammad's Elasticsearch requirements.

The Elasticsearch service is optional. Without it, Zammad searches the database, which is slower and less complete. To save resources, leave it out when you create the app. To turn Elasticsearch off while the service is still linked, set the environment variable ELASTICSEARCH_ENABLED to false on the Zammad app service.

Wodby writes Zammad's Elasticsearch settings on every deployment, from the link, so changes made to them in Zammad are overwritten. When no search index exists, the deployment builds one.

docs.title: Mail
docs.text:
Zammad sends agent notifications through its notification channel. While the Zammad app service is linked to OpenSMTPD, Wodby points Zammad's unconfigured notification channel at the relay. For production delivery, attach an SMTP provider integration to OpenSMTPD. See the OpenSMTPD guide.

You can also set your mail provider's SMTP server as the notification sender directly in Zammad under Admin > Channels > Email. Wodby never changes a notification channel that you have configured in Zammad.

Incoming email is not configured by Wodby. To turn messages into tickets, add your mailboxes under Admin > Channels > Email. See Zammad's email channel documentation.

docs.title: Domains
docs.text:
Zammad builds links in notifications from the app service's primary domain, and only allows live connections from it. Wodby sets this address on every deployment, so changes made to it in Zammad are overwritten. After you change the primary domain, deploy the Zammad app service again.

The browser keeps WebSocket connections open, so the route has no request timeout by default. Do not set the route's request body size: it makes the route hold each request in memory until it is complete, and live connections stop working. See HTTP settings.

docs.title: Change configuration
docs.text: Add environment variables through the Zammad app service's Additional Zammad environment variables integration, then deploy. Every Zammad process receives them. Useful ones include TZ, ZAMMAD_WEB_CONCURRENCY, MAX_THREADS, and ZAMMAD_PROCESS_DELAYED_JOBS_WORKERS. See Environment variables.

docs.title: Data and backups
docs.text:
• PostgreSQL (20 GB volume by default) holds tickets, users, settings, and attachments.
  • Elasticsearch (10 GB volume by default) holds the search index, which Zammad can rebuild from the database.
  • Redis has a 1 GB volume. Memcached keeps its cache in memory only.
  • The Zammad service has no volume.

Zammad stores attachments in the database by default, so back up the PostgreSQL database. The PostgreSQL service has backup and import operations in Wodby. The Zammad, Redis, Memcached, Elasticsearch, and OpenSMTPD services have none. See Backups and Imports.

To keep attachments in S3-compatible storage instead, add the S3_URL variable through the Additional Zammad environment variables integration, deploy, then choose S3 under Admin > System > Storage. See Zammad's storage settings. File system storage is not supported, because Zammad's processes share no volume. With S3, back up the bucket together with the database.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Every Zammad process runs one replica, and the service does not scale. The background worker must never run twice, so it is replaced, not updated in place, on each deployment.
  • Imports from other helpdesks (OTRS, Zendesk, Freshdesk, Kayako) on Zammad's getting started page are not available, because Wodby has already set up the system.

docs.title: ZooKeeper stack guide
docs.text:
The Wodby ZooKeeper catalog stack runs a ZooKeeper service. The current composition and defaults are in wodby/stack-zookeeper.

In Wodby stacks, ZooKeeper is the coordination store of SolrCloud. Applications normally do not talk to it directly. See the Solr guide.

docs.title: Connect a service
docs.text:
Use these values from a service in the same app environment:

  • Host: the ZooKeeper app service name
  • Client port: 2181

No client authentication or TLS is configured, and Wodby generates no token. Only the environment's internal network reaches the service. A linked Solr service uses the host as its ZK_HOST and protects its own znodes with digest credentials.

docs.title: Change configuration
docs.text:
On every start, the container builds its zoo.cfg from environment variables. With one replica, ZooKeeper runs standalone. Do not edit the file. Set environment variables on the app service instead:

Variable Setting Default ZOO_TICK_TIME, ZOO_INIT_LIMIT, ZOO_SYNC_LIMIT tickTime, initLimit, syncLimit 2000, 5, 2 ZOO_MAX_CLIENT_CNXNS maxClientCnxns 60 ZOO_AUTOPURGE_PURGE_INTERVAL, ZOO_AUTOPURGE_SNAP_RETAIN_COUNT Snapshot auto-purge 0 (off), 3 ZOO_4LW_COMMANDS_WHITELIST Allowed four-letter commands stat,ruok,conf,isro

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
Snapshots are in /data, and the transaction log is in /data/datalog on the same volume.

The Data volume is optional, and the stack does not define one. Without it, data is lost when the container is replaced. For SolrCloud, that includes the collections' configuration, config sets, and security settings. They live in ZooKeeper and not on Solr's volume. Wodby defines no backups or imports for this service.

docs.title: Check that ZooKeeper is running
docs.text:
Open a web terminal for the ZooKeeper app service and run:

echo ruok | nc -w 2 localhost 2181

It answers imok. make stat -f /usr/local/bin/actions.mk prints the server mode and connected clients.

docs.title: User settings
docs.text:
User settings contain personal account and security controls that apply to your Wodby user, not just to a single project.

Open them from your avatar menu in the dashboard.

docs.title: Sections
docs.text:
• Account for your profile and account deletion
  • Preferences for dashboard appearance and your default organization
  • Emails for primary and secondary email addresses
  • Notifications for personal email notification preferences per organization
  • Security for password changes, two-factor authentication, and recovery codes
  • Identities for linked sign-in providers
  • SSH keys for public keys propagated to supported SSHD services
  • API keys for personal automation tokens scoped to an organization

docs.title: Organization-aware settings
docs.text:
Most user settings are personal. Some personal settings are also tied to an organization:

  • the default organization controls which organization opens after signing in or visiting the dashboard home page
  • notification preferences are personal email settings for one selected organization
  • every API key is created for one specific organization

docs.title: Related pages
docs.text:

docs.title: Account
docs.text: The Account page in user settings is the basic profile page for your Wodby user.

docs.title: What you can do
docs.text:
• update your display name
  • delete your account

docs.title: Deleting your account
docs.text: Account deletion is handled from the same page and should be treated as a permanent action. Review organization membership, access, and automation that depends on your user before deleting it.

docs.title: Related pages

docs.title: API keys
docs.text:
Create API keys from User settings > API keys.

These keys are intended for automation with the Wodby API and CLI.

docs.title: When creating a key
docs.text:
You choose:

  • organization
  • description
  • expiration: No expiration, 1 month, 3 months, or 6 months

Each key belongs to one organization. If you automate against multiple organizations, create a separate key for each one.

docs.title: After creation
docs.text:
• The token value is shown only once.
  • Store it securely before leaving the page.
  • The dashboard later shows metadata such as creation time, last use, and expiry.

docs.title: Managing existing keys
docs.text:
From the list page you can:

  • review description
  • review creation time
  • review last-use time
  • review expiry
  • delete the key

docs.title: Emails
docs.text:
Manage your email addresses from User settings > Emails.

The page shows which address is primary and whether each address is verified.

docs.title: What you can do
docs.text:
• add a secondary email
  • verify a newly added email
  • promote a verified secondary email to primary
  • delete a non-primary email

docs.title: Important rules
docs.text:
• only verified secondary emails can become the primary email
  • the primary email cannot be deleted directly
  • adding or deleting an email, or changing your primary email, may ask you to confirm it's you
  • these changes aren't available with an API key

docs.title: Related pages
docs.text:

docs.title: Identities
docs.text:
The Identities page lists external sign-in providers linked to your Wodby user.

The dashboard can show linked identities such as:

  • Google
  • GitHub
  • organization SSO providers

For each linked identity, Wodby shows the associated email address and lets you unlink that identity. Unlinking may ask you to confirm it's you.

Organization SSO identities are created when you sign in through an organization's configured SSO provider.

Google Workspace SSO and GitHub Organization SSO identities are separate from personal Google and GitHub sign-in identities. Signing in through organization SSO does not automatically link the regular Google or GitHub sign-in method to your Wodby user.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text:
Manage email notification preferences from User settings > Notifications.

Notification settings are personal to your Wodby user. They are also scoped to one organization at a time.

docs.title: Choosing an organization
docs.text:
Use the organization selector at the top of the page to choose which organization's email notifications you want to configure.

Changing a notification setting affects only:

  • your user account
  • the selected organization
  • the specific notification type you changed

It does not change notification delivery for other organization members.

docs.title: What you can configure
docs.text:
The page groups notification types by category, such as apps, clusters, automation, integrations, billing, and reports.

Each optional notification has its own toggle. Turning a notification off stops that type of email for your user in the selected organization.

Examples include:

  • failed app builds or deployments
  • app creation results
  • cluster creation or connection events
  • successful or failed automatic cluster infrastructure and Kubernetes version upgrades
  • automatic service source updates, inherited-service base revision updates, Git-backed stack updates, stack service revision updates, origin stack syncs, and app stack upgrades
  • cron job and backup failures and recoveries, plus failed imports, certificate renewals, custom certificate expiration, service actions, or integration installs
  • breached spending limits
  • weekly organization reports

docs.title: Security infrastructure upgrade notices (upcoming)
docs.text:
Wodby may send critical security upgrade notices to organization members who have permission to upgrade affected clusters. These notices are separate from optional upgrade result emails and are not disabled by the notification toggles or newsletter preferences.

A notice identifies clusters you can upgrade and explains the required action. The upcoming K3s host CA security update applies only to self-hosted K3s servers. Check the cluster's current version and task history before acting: an automatic upgrade may have completed since the notice was prepared.

docs.title: Scheduled cron and backup notifications
docs.text:
The Cron job failures and recoveries and Backup failures and recoveries settings control both failure and recovery emails for scheduled automation:

  • Cron jobs: Wodby emails organization admins on the first failure, then at most once every 24 hours when further runs fail. Repeated-failure emails use Scheduled cron job still failing. A new failure after a successful run sends an immediate email.
  • Backups: Each failed scheduled occurrence sends an email. Repeated-failure emails use Scheduled backup still failing.
  • Recovery: The first later conclusive success sends a recovery email immediately.

Cron and backup execution schedules stay as configured. Failure logs and emails include the next scheduled attempt when available; disabled or overdue schedules are identified separately. If you change the schedule afterward, the next run can differ from the time in an earlier message.

An automatic backup preset can create several backup artifacts in one scheduled occurrence. Any failed artifact makes the occurrence fail, but recovery is reported only after every artifact in a later occurrence completes successfully.

A failed manual cron job or backup still emails the user who started it.

docs.title: Certificate renewal notifications
docs.text:
For automatic Let's Encrypt renewal, Wodby notifies organization admins after every failed attempt. The first email uses Certificate renewal failed; later failures use Certificate renewal still failing.

Retry delays increase with consecutive failures: 1 day, 2 days, 3 days, 4 days, 5 days, 6 days, then 7 days between attempts. Further retries stay seven days apart. A small offset spreads attempts across certificates, and a longer certificate-authority retry delay takes precedence. Successful renewal resets the failure history.

If a certificate expires before the next retry, Wodby schedules one additional renewal attempt at expiry, or when the app and cluster next become eligible. A later retry time required by the certificate authority still takes precedence. After this attempt, the ordinary backoff resumes.

If the certificate is already expired when a failure email is prepared, its subject says Certificate expired; renewal failed. The Cloudflare action suffix remains when that attempt confirmed a browser challenge. Emails covering both expired and valid certificates explicitly identify that the batch includes expired certificates.

Failure task logs and emails include the next scheduled retry time. The relative delay is measured when the message is generated; it is not a countdown that updates in your inbox. Correct external validation problems before expiry, using the troubleshooting links below.

The first successful automatic retry after previous failures sends a Certificate renewal recovered email. The certificate renewal notification preference controls both failure and recovery emails. If a task renews several certificates, recovery is reported for the certificates that recovered, even if others still failed.

If a notification identifies a Cloudflare browser challenge, follow the Cloudflare troubleshooting steps. See certificate troubleshooting for other validation errors.

docs.title: Custom certificate expiration notifications
docs.text: The Custom certificate expiration setting controls warnings for uploaded TLS certificates, which Wodby does not renew automatically. Wodby emails organization admins 30, 14, 7, and 1 day before expiration and once after the certificate expires. Each stage is sent once for a certificate's current expiration date.

docs.title: Weekly organization report
docs.text:
Organization owners and admins get a weekly email that sums up the organization's previous week: items that need attention, failed automation, automatic updates, outdated stacks and clusters, activity, and access and security issues.

To stop or restart it for an organization, use the weekly organization report toggle on this page, or the unsubscribe link in the email.

docs.title: Defaults
docs.text:
Notifications are enabled by default unless you turn them off.

If you have not saved a preference for a notification type yet, Wodby treats it as enabled.

docs.title: Access
docs.text: Notification settings are available to users who can view the selected organization. The settings are the same regardless of your organization role because they control your own email preferences, not organization-wide behavior.

docs.title: Email unsubscribe links
docs.text: Unsubscribe links in notification emails update the same personal, organization-scoped setting shown on this page.

docs.title: Preferences
docs.text: The Preferences page contains settings that control how the dashboard opens and appears for your user.

docs.title: Appearance
docs.text: Choose System to follow your device color theme, or select Light or Dark explicitly. The theme preference is stored in the current browser, so you can use a different theme on another browser or device.

docs.title: Default organization
docs.text:
Choose which organization Wodby opens after you sign in or visit the dashboard home page.

Only organizations where you have an active membership are available. If that membership is removed, Wodby clears the default organization until you choose another one.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: The Security section in user settings covers password management, two-factor authentication, and recovery codes.

docs.title: Password
docs.text:
You can change your password from User settings > Security.

To change your password, enter your current one. If your account has no password yet, for example because you sign in with Google or GitHub, setting the first one needs a recent confirmation.

docs.title: Changes to how you sign in
docs.text:
These changes affect who can sign in to your whole account, so Wodby asks you to confirm it's you if you haven't signed in or confirmed during the last five minutes:

  • setting a first password
  • enabling or disabling 2FA
  • generating new recovery codes
  • adding or deleting an email address, or changing your primary email
  • unlinking a sign-in identity
  • deleting an account that has no password

You confirm in the same way as for a secret reveal.

These changes are only available in a signed-in browser session. API keys and tokens can't make them, or change a password or delete an account, and get an error instead.

docs.title: Secret reveal confirmation
docs.text:
Displaying a stored app or database credential requires an interactive user session and the appropriate secret reveal permission.

When you click a reveal action, Wodby opens a dialog and checks whether you signed in or completed another confirmation during the last five minutes. If additional confirmation is needed, the dialog uses an authentication method available for your account:

  • accounts with 2FA enter an authenticator or recovery code
  • other accounts with a Wodby password confirm their current password
  • other passwordless accounts receive a six-digit code at their verified primary email address

An email code expires after five minutes, and requests and verification attempts are limited. After confirmation, the secret is displayed for 30 seconds and is then removed from the dialog. Closing the dialog removes it immediately.

Secret reveal responses are not cached. API-key and token authentication cannot use direct reveal operations.

Copying a value places it on your device's clipboard; Wodby cannot clear that copy automatically. Move long-lived credentials into an approved secrets manager and rotate any value that may have been exposed.

docs.title: Two-factor authentication
docs.text: Wodby supports two-factor authentication with a one-time password authenticator app.

docs.title: Enrolling in 2FA
docs.text:
The enrollment flow is:

  1. confirm it's you, if you haven't recently
  2. save the generated recovery codes
  3. scan the QR code or enter the secret manually in your authenticator app
  4. enter the 6-digit verification code

Recovery codes are shown before final verification so you can store them safely.

docs.title: Wodby Registry with 2FA
docs.text: docker login cannot ask for a one-time code, so Wodby Registry does not accept the password of an account with 2FA. Sign in with your email and an API key as the password. See Wodby Registry.

docs.title: Disabling 2FA
docs.text: Disabling 2FA also requires a recent confirmation.

docs.title: Recovery codes
docs.text:
Recovery codes are managed from the same security area.

  • recovery codes are only shown when they are generated
  • generating new codes requires a recent confirmation
  • when you generate new codes, replace your previously stored set

docs.text:

docs.title: SSH keys
docs.text:
Manage your SSH public keys from User settings > SSH keys.

These keys are propagated to supported SSHD app services that you can modify.

docs.title: What happens when you add or remove a key
docs.text:
Wodby adds your SSH keys to SSHD app services with a published port in apps where you have writable access.

Changing your SSH keys triggers redeployment of those SSHD services so the updated authorized keys can be applied.

docs.title: Development workspaces
docs.text: Development workspaces use the owner's registered keys for their personal SSH runner. Other users with writable app access do not receive workspace SSH access. Key changes refresh access and end active runner sessions; an unreachable cluster can delay that refresh.

docs.title: Supported key formats
docs.text:
The dashboard accepts the following public key types:

  • ssh-rsa
  • ssh-ed25519
  • ecdsa-sha2-nistp256
  • ecdsa-sha2-nistp384
  • ecdsa-sha2-nistp521

docs.title: Key details
docs.text:
The key details page shows the key fingerprint and lets you delete the key.

Deleting a key also triggers redeployment of affected SSHD services.
